title: Mortgage broker
tagline: Learn to guide borrowers from first enquiry to a committed application with the right lender.
setting: Conversations happen in your office, on the phone and occasionally at a client’s kitchen table, moving from fact-find to recommendation to full application.

scenarios.label: First fact-find call
scenarios.desc: A new lead asks what rates you can get and whether you charge a fee.
scenarios.setup: The borrower is sitting at their kitchen table with a laptop open on Rightmove. They say: Hi, I saw your site, what’s the best two-year fixed you can find and do you charge a fee?
scenarios.objective: Book a 30-minute fact-find meeting and agree the fee structure in principle.
scenarios.moment: Tuesday 10:15 am, morning light through the blinds

scenarios.label: Lender recommendation meeting
scenarios.desc: You present two lender options and the borrower pushes back on rate, fee and speed.
scenarios.setup: The borrowers are a couple in their early thirties at your desk with payslips and bank statements printed. One says: The high-street bank offered 4.39 per cent with no broker fee, why should we pay you five hundred quid and take 4.54 per cent?
scenarios.objective: Secure a decision in principle on your recommended lender and a signed client agreement.
scenarios.moment: Thursday 6:20 pm, rain tapping the window

scenarios.label: Full application and valuation hurdle
scenarios.desc: The borrower hesitates to pay the valuation fee after a down-valuation scare on a forum.
scenarios.setup: The borrower is back at your desk, decision in principle in hand. They say: I’ve read horror stories about down-valuations, if I pay three hundred for the valuation and it comes in low, I’ve lost the lot.
scenarios.objective: Collect the valuation fee, submit the full application and book the surveyor.
scenarios.moment: Monday 5:50 pm, low winter sun through the blinds

buyers.angle: Eager but uncertain about long-term commitment.
Prioritizes rate savings over service quality.

buyers.role: investment property purchaser needing multiple loans
buyers.angle: Requires complex structuring and fast approvals.
Needs quick loan approvals to secure multiple properties.

objections: I can’t get approved with my current credit score
The interest rates feel too high compared to my other options
I don’t understand the loan terms and need them explained simply
I’m concerned about hidden fees I haven’t considered
My income is irregular and I worry it might disqualify me
I need to know how long the approval process will take
I want to know if I can pay off the loan early without penalties
I need to compare rates from multiple lenders before deciding

rubric.label: Fact-find
rubric.what: You uncover income, deposit, credit, property type and timeline before quoting any product.

rubric.label: Fee transparency
rubric.what: You state your fee, when it is payable and any lender procuration fee clearly and early.

rubric.label: Lender match
rubric.what: You explain why the recommended lender fits the borrower’s profile better than the high-street alternative.

rubric.label: Rate context
rubric.what: You frame rate differences in monthly pounds and total cost over the deal term, not just headline percent.

rubric.label: Risk framing
rubric.what: You set out valuation risk, mortgage conditions and fallback options without minimising or exaggerating.

rubric.label: Compliance record
rubric.what: You confirm the borrower understands the fee, the lender’s charges and the illustration is not an offer, and you note it on file.

pitfalls: Quoting a rate before completing a full fact-find.
Presenting a lender illustration as a guaranteed offer.
Failing to disclose the broker fee and any procuration fee before the client agreement is signed.
line: Selling mortgages as a mortgage broker

research.text: The sources provide insights into common objections faced by homebuyers and how to address them, but do not specifically detail objections and responses in the context of selling mortgages as a mortgage broker. The realtor.com article discusses common homebuyer objections rooted in fear and uncertainty, emphasizing the importance of understanding and guiding clients through their concerns. The Yahoo Finance articles on Doncaster Mortgage Broker focus on the company's services and expansion but do not delve into specific objections or sales strategies in the mortgage brokering field. Therefore, the sources do not provide a definitive answer to the question about common customer objections and how conversations go when selling mortgages as a mortgage broker.
